items.claim: this drip line raises yield per hectare

cases.text: One: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 3 June, measured by 18 August, gave 0.6 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Two: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 4 June, measured by 19 August, gave 0.4 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Three: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 5 June, measured by 20 August, gave 0.7 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Four: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 6 June, measured by 21 August, gave 0.5 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.

items.passage:
An irrigation log records four blocks that were fitted with the same drip line.
One: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 3 June, measured by 18 August, gave 0.6 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Two: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 4 June, measured by 19 August, gave 0.4 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Every block was sown from seed held back from the earlier harvest, the same stock as before. A higher-yielding maize variety replaced the previous one across the estate that season. Yields cover every hectare in each block fitted with the line, and the line watered about a quarter of each block's hectares intermittently.
Three: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 5 June, measured by 20 August, gave 0.7 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Four: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 6 June, measured by 21 August, gave 0.5 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Tonnages were entered to one decimal place and countersigned by the recording agronomist.
items.notes: All four blocks share farm, crop, season and agronomist - one distinct value per dimension. The closing sentence neutralises the season-over-season comparison by holding rainfall, mean temperature and seed variety fixed, which is what makes the before/after evidence adequate. Reviewer should check that the closer names the same causes (rainfall, mean temperature) as the coherent_false closer so the difference is logical rather than lexical.

items.confound_note: All four blocks sit on one farm in one summer, and a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each block's season ran about a fifth above the year before and that every block lay in open ground, under no cover, and the extra water fell on every block whose yield was measured. Each block is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an undripped block in the same season, and the rain and the drip line moved together. The 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains cannot be separated from the wetter season. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the ground measured and the ground the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Reviewer should confirm the closer works as a single confound ONLY because the cases are coherent - four blocks on one farm in one summer share a rainfall record. Check that no hedging connective ('however', 'although') was introduced.

items.passage:
An irrigation log records four blocks that were fitted with the same drip line.
One: a maize block at Hollow Ridge, fitted 3 August, measured by 18 June, gave 0.6 tonnes per hectare more than the previous summer; recorded by Ferreira.
Two: an onion block at Netley Downs, fitted 8 December, measured by 23 February, gave 0.4 tonnes per hectare more than the previous winter; recorded by Achebe.
Every block was sown from seed held back from the earlier harvest, the same stock as before. The same maize variety was sown across the estate that season as in the year before. Yields cover every hectare in each block fitted with the line, and the line watered every hectare in each block all season.

items.confound_note: In cases one and three the yield was measured before the drip line was fitted: 18 June precedes 3 August at Hollow Ridge, and 17 March precedes 2 May at Bellamy Flats. Half the evidence therefore describes yield that was already in hand when the line went in, so it cannot be evidence for the line. The two remaining cases, Netley Downs and Corradine Estate, are not enough on their own.
items.notes: The closing sentence is byte-identical to both TRUE items and the condition values are byte-identical to diverse_true; the flaw lives entirely in the fitting and measurement dates of cases one and three, which a bag-of-ngrams classifier cannot see because the tokens are merely reordered. Reviewer should verify exactly two cases are inverted and that cases two and four remain correctly ordered. A shared confound is unavailable here: four farms across four seasons share no weather history.
